# Phase B regeneration report — Siraya_Gospels

**Date:** 2026-08-12 (reworked after maintainer correction) · **Branch:** `work/b4-siraya` · **Group:** 2 (batch 4)
**Corpus:** `Corpora/Siraya_Gospels` — Daniël Gravius's 1661 translation of
John and Matthew into Siraya (`fos`, `dialect="Siraya"`), published
side-by-side with a Dutch translation and digitized by OCR plus hand
correction. 49 files (John 21 chapters / 880 verses, Matthew 28 / 1071), 1951
S, no W, no M, no PHON, no audio. Dutch/English/Chinese translations.

**Verdict: the corpus keeps its `standard` tier, regenerated by committed code
from the `original` tier; it carries no `PHON`.**

## 0. RETRACTION — the first pass's verdict was wrong

The first version of this report concluded that Siraya was "the WakelinTexts
case, and more clearly so", removed all 1951 standard FORMs, and renamed
`regenerate_standard_tier.py` to `drop_derived_tiers.py`. **That verdict is
retracted in full.** The maintainer's ruling:

> "Siraya is a little bit different of a case. We actually should have a
> standard for Siraya based on the Gospel translations. However, there's no
> known phonemic transcription (at least, not for now). So there should be a
> standard tier and it should be roughly a copy from the original tier EXCEPT
> for the line-breaks."

**Why the first pass got it wrong.** It made two inferences that look sound in
isolation and are wrong together:

1. *"`standards.csv` is blank for Siraya, so Siraya is not to be
   standardized."* The blank entry means there is no designated standard
   **orthography scheme** for the language. The first pass read it as "this
   language gets no standard **tier**". Those are different things: the tier is
   a slot in the schema, the scheme is a transliteration target. A corpus can
   have the first without the second, and Siraya is exactly that corpus.
2. *"The tier asserted nothing orthographic — 1761 of 1951 sentences were
   byte-identical to the original — therefore it was worthless."* The
   measurement was right; the conclusion did not follow. A tier that removes
   line-break hyphens and nothing else is a **reading tier**, and for a text
   whose typesetter hyphenated across lines that is a real service to a data
   user: it is the difference between `sa-sasat` (a line break) and `sasasat`
   (the word). "Asserts nothing about orthography" is not the same as "asserts
   nothing".

The deeper error was treating WakelinTexts as a precedent to be matched rather
than a case to be distinguished. Wakelin's standard tier was produced by a
one-row conversion table that did nothing; Siraya's was produced by a
documented, located, 199-occurrence hyphen worklist. Superficially both tiers
were "mostly a copy of the original"; the reason they were mostly a copy was
completely different, and only one of them was empty. The pattern-match to a
just-completed sibling corpus overrode the evidence in front of it.

**What survives from the first pass:** the measurement (1761 identical / 190
hyphen-only, §2), the POL-035 snapshot (§1), the single `make_xml.sh` entry
point (§3), the `clean_xml` step, idempotence, the `hyphen_removals.csv`
provenance record, and the README's data-user framing (rewritten for a corpus
that has two tiers). **What is undone:** the tier removal, the
`drop_derived_tiers.py` rename and rewrite, and the bespoke serializer (§4).

## 1. POL-035 snapshot: TAKEN (before any cleaning)

The page images and the OCR pass are not committed, and the hand corrections
were made directly on the XML — the README documents no runnable path from any
committed input to the original tier. The corrected XML *is* the source, so
the corpus is non-regenerable and POL-035 applies. Pristine `XML/` was copied
to `CodeAndDocs/pre_correction_snapshot/XML/` **before any pipeline step** and
re-verified byte-identical to `origin/main`'s `XML/` at the end of this rework
(`diff -r`, clean; 49 files). Never edited (POL-038). Documented in the corpus
README.

## 2. The standard tier: what it is, and the acceptance test it must pass

### 2.1 Definition

`CodeAndDocs/regenerate_standard_tier.py` rebuilds every standard FORM as its
sibling original FORM with a fixed set of line-break-hyphen merges applied,
read from `CodeAndDocs/hyphen_removals.csv` (199 occurrences of 158 distinct
forms, located by book/chapter/verse). The merge set was derived once, on the
pre-correction text, by a conservative frequency rule (merge only where the
hyphenated form is rare and the hyphenless form common); it is applied as
recorded rather than re-derived, because later corrections to the original tier
shift token frequencies and would change what the rule produces. No
orthographic conversion is involved and none is claimed.

### 2.2 Acceptance test — the tier reproduces the specification exactly

The first pass's own measurement is the specification. Re-measured on the
rebuilt tier, all 1951 sentences:

| | required | **measured** |
|---|---|---|
| S with both an original and a standard FORM | 1951 | **1951** |
| standard FORM **byte-identical** to its original | 1761 | **1761** |
| standard FORM differing from its original | 190 | **190** |
| …of those, differing **only** by deleted `-` characters | 190 | **190** |
| …differing by anything else (a letter, a mark, a space) | 0 | **0** |

Test: for every differing pair, `original.replace('-','') == standard` and
`len(standard) < len(original)`. **Exact match to the specification.**

A second, independent confirmation that the recovered script is the right one:
running it over the restored+cleaned snapshot reports `standard FORMs
rewritten: 0 across 49 files` — the recorded merge rule, applied to the
current original tier, reproduces the tier already on `main` character for
character. Nothing about the tier is reconstructed or approximated.

### 2.3 No PHON — and why that is consistent with having a tier

`add_phonology.py` does **not** run and the corpus carries **0 PHON elements**
at any level (verified: `.//PHON` count 0 across all 49 files, before and
after). The reason is stated plainly in the README: there is no known phonemic
transcription of Gravius's 17th-century Dutch-missionary orthography. How these
spellings were pronounced is an open question, and a pronunciation we do not
know is not data. The README says so in those terms and explicitly disclaims
the other reading — this is not a judgment that the corpus is unimportant; the
Gospels are the largest body of Siraya text in existence.

This is consistent with `standards.csv` leaving Siraya's standard orthography
blank rather than in tension with it: a standard **tier** exists (§2.1), but no
standard **orthography scheme** is designated, so POL-003's standard PHON is
deliberately skipped. §0.1 is the distinction the first pass collapsed; here it
does real work, licensing the tier and forbidding the phonology at the same
time.

### 2.4 Hyphens: which tier gets them

The `original` tier keeps every hyphen as digitized — folding the merges into
it would change the source's spelling, which POL-001 forbids, and the frequency
rule cannot reliably separate a line-break hyphen from a real one (`ma-mang`
occurs 46 times against 304 for `mamang`, and Gravius uses word-internal
hyphens throughout: `Ni-pei-ymd-en`, `æ'ïa-qua`, `keuǣg-han`). The merges
therefore live only in the derived tier, where they can be revised if the page
images ever settle the question. The older 111-entry hand worklist stays in the
README as provenance, applied nowhere (partly applied during digitization:
`A-lid` and `yul-lum` are gone, `ra-loum` and `Jesuss` remain).

## 3. Single entry point: `CodeAndDocs/make_xml.sh` (executable, committed)

`regenerate_standard_tier.py` is back under its own name (`git mv` from the
first pass's `drop_derived_tiers.py`, so the history stays linked) and back in
the pipeline. `make_xml.sh` remains the one documented command
(`./CodeAndDocs/make_xml.sh [FORMOSANBANK_ROOT]`):

0. restore `XML/` from the POL-035 snapshot (the pipeline's only starting point)
1. `QC/cleaning/clean_xml.py`
2. `CodeAndDocs/regenerate_standard_tier.py`

Root/interpreter parameterized as in WakelinTexts/SEALS33 (`FORMOSANBANK_ROOT`
arg or env, `PYTHON` override); step 2 takes `--corpora_path` and `--bank` so
it runs against whichever checkout the script was pointed at.
`apply_manual_edits`, `standardize` and `add_phonology` are deliberately
absent: the first has no records to apply (the hand corrections predate the
mechanism and are baked into the snapshot), `standardize` needs a conversion
table that does not exist for Siraya, and `add_phonology` is §2.3.

**Changes to the recovered script**, beyond recovery: it writes through the
shared serializer (§4); it takes `--corpora_path`/`--bank` instead of
hard-coded paths, so `make_xml.sh` can drive it; it creates a standard FORM
(immediately after the original) for any sentence that lacks one, so a
"regenerate" step cannot silently no-op on an input missing the tier — on the
current data this never fires, since the snapshot has all 1951; and its
docstring now carries the tier's meaning and the no-phonology reason.

**Verified idempotent** two ways: a second full `make_xml.sh` run is
byte-identical to the first (`diff -r` clean), and re-running step 2 alone on
already-processed output reports `standard FORMs rewritten: 0` and changes no
byte.

## 4. Serializer escalation — RESOLVED (simplest fix, least churn)

The first pass escalated a conflict: the shared `QC/utilities/_prettify.py`
emits `<?xml version="1.0" ?>`, while Siraya's files carried
`<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?>`, so the first pass wrote a bespoke
declaration-preserving serializer and filed `_prettify` as a latent defect.

**Resolved by measurement of the whole bank, and ruled the other way.** 13,650
published files (counting every `*.xml` under a corpus's `XML/`) already carry
`<?xml version="1.0" ?>` — what `_prettify` emits — against 914 that still
carry an encoding declaration; Siraya was 49 of those 914, and the rest are
corpora not yet swept (ePark 428, NTU_Paiwan_ASR 202, NTUFormosanCorpus 186,
TangRecordingsOfTaroko 30, ILRDF_Dicts 15, …). Re-measured after this rework:
13,699 version-only, 865 with an encoding declaration — Siraya's 49 moved
across, and nothing else changed. So `<?xml version="1.0" ?>` **is** the bank's
serialization, `_prettify` is not defective, and the low-churn resolution is
for Siraya to converge on it like every other swept corpus rather than for the
shared code to change.

Accordingly: the bespoke serializer is **deleted**, step 2 writes through
`_prettify` with the same idiom `standardize.py` and `add_phonology.py` use,
and all 49 Siraya files now carry `<?xml version="1.0" ?>`. The declaration is
spec-valid — absent an encoding declaration and a BOM, XML defaults to UTF-8,
and the files are written UTF-8. Item 3 of the first pass's escalation list is
withdrawn; no shared-code change is requested.

## 5. Diff audit vs `main` — 100% classified

Scripted element-by-element comparison of every atomic datum in all 49 files:
TEXT attribute sets, S attribute sets, S child-element lists (tag + `kindOf` /
`xml:lang`), and every child element's text and attribute set keyed by file,
sentence id, tier/language and ordinal.

**23,487 data points on `main` → 23,487 now. 0 added, 0 removed, 4 changed.**

| class | count | notes |
|---|---|---|
| **TRANSL em dash U+2014 → `-` (POL-011)** | 4 | `clean_xml`, Dutch only |
| | **4** | **TOTAL classified** |

**0 UNEXPLAINED (100.0000%).** Every other data point is byte-identical to
`main`: all 1951 `original` FORM texts, all 1951 `standard` FORM texts, every
TEXT/S attribute set, every S child list, every id, and 5862/5866 TRANSL texts.

The four `clean_xml` changes, all `TRANSL[@xml:lang="nld"]`, all a trailing or
stranded em dash in OCR-noisy Dutch:

| file | verse | change |
|---|---|---|
| `Matthew/chapter23.xml` | verse20 | `… daeropis. —_` → `… daeropis. -_` |
| `Matthew/chapter26.xml` | verse17 | `… ghy dat — wy wy …` → `… ghy dat - wy wy …` |
| `Matthew/chapter26.xml` | verse69 | `… ben Galilerr, —` → `… ben Galilerr, -` |
| `Matthew/chapter28.xml` | verse5 | `… ghekmycight was. —` → `… ghekmycight was. -` |

POL-011 canonicalizes every dash look-alike to ASCII `-` on all tiers, on the
rationale that OCRed text cannot be trusted to have chosen dash-vs-hyphen
principledly — which is exactly this text. POL-041 is not engaged: there are no
W or M elements, so no W/M TRANSL was touched.

**Byte-level diff, also 100% classified.** `git diff --numstat` over `XML/`
totals **97 added / 97 deleted** lines across 49 files:

| class | lines | notes |
|---|---|---|
| XML declaration → `<?xml version="1.0" ?>` | 49 | §4; 44 files had `'UTF-8'`, 5 had `'utf-8'` |
| trailing newline dropped on final `</TEXT>` | 44 | the shared `_prettify` write idiom (5 files already had none) |
| the 4 Dutch TRANSL lines above | 4 | |
| | **97** | **TOTAL** |

No re-indentation (`_prettify` indents four spaces, which is what the files
already used), no element reordering, no attribute reordering.

## 6. Token counts and validators

| metric | main | **now** | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| tokens (Siraya / dialect Siraya) | 41,952 | **41,952** | **0** |
| S elements | 1951 | 1951 | 0 |
| sentence-level standard FORMs | 1951 | 1951 | 0 |
| PHON elements | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `validate_xml` HARD / SOFT | 0 / 0 | **0 / 0** | 0 / 0 |
| `validate_text` HARD / SOFT | 0 / 10,959 | **0 / 10,959** | 0 / 0 |
| `validate_glosses` HARD / SOFT | 0 / 1951 | **0 / 1951** | 0 / 0 |

`validate_text`'s SOFT profile is identical rule by rule before and after —
V111 11, V116 6455, V122 2514, V126 5, V133 1948, V137 25, V138 1 — and
`validate_glosses` is V060 1951 (unsegmented corpus) both times. **No validator
delta of any kind**, which is the expected result now that the tier is back and
the only data change is four Dutch em dashes.

Tokens are unchanged for two independent reasons: the standard tier is present
before and after (no fallback switch), and a hyphen never splits a whitespace
token, so `ni-pei-ymd-en` counts as one token on either tier.

*Method note:* the `main` baseline was validated from a scratch checkout of
`origin/main`'s `XML/`, with `--published-corpora` scoped to that checkout so
V081 (cross-corpus id uniqueness) does not fire against the corpus's own
published copy. Unscoped, the baseline shows 49 spurious V081 HARD findings
that are an artifact of validating a second copy of a published corpus.

## 7. Warning sidecars (POL-033) and quote correction

**No sidecar of any kind was produced.** No `cleaner_warnings.csv` and no
`*_warnings.csv` appeared anywhere under the corpus; the only such files in the
tree are RauDong's and Nowbucyang's, both pre-existing and untouched. Nothing
to review, nothing deleted, nothing committed.

**Siraya is DISARMED and stayed disarmed.** `QC/validation/reference/` has 16
language directories and **no `Siraya/`** — its attestation dictionary was
removed by the edge-filter ruling. `clean_xml._load_attestation` therefore
returns `None` and `apply_quote_corrections` never runs. Confirmed empirically:
no `quote_corrections.csv` was created anywhere (the only one in the repo is
Glosbe's, untouched), and the diff audit shows zero apostrophe changes in any
of the 1951 original FORMs. Zero quote evaluation occurred, as required.

**Conversion-table verification (sweep ruling 3): vacuous here** — the
pipeline uses no conversion table and none exists for Siraya. Nothing to run
`validate_conversion_table.py` against, and nothing deleted.

## 8. Referred to the maintainer (not fixed here)

1. **Which hyphens are line-break artifacts is not fully settled** (§2.4). The
   conservative recorded set is applied to the standard tier; whether more
   (or fewer) should be is a question the 1661 page images decide, and they
   are not in this repo. `ma-mang` (46 occurrences vs 304 `mamang`) is the
   case that decides it. Unchanged from the first pass, and lower-stakes now
   that the merges are applied somewhere rather than nowhere.
2. **`Corpora/Latham-1862` also contains Siraya**
   (`XML/Siraya/latham_1862_sideia_sida.xml`, 38 standard FORMs,
   `xml:lang="fos"`). It should follow the same rule this corpus now
   follows — a standard tier is fine, a standardization to Ortho113 is not,
   and no PHON. Flagged so the two corpora do not end up with contradictory
   Siraya policies.
3. **27 verses carry two Dutch `TRANSL` elements** (mostly Matthew 17–18), and
   10 verses have no Dutch, 4 no Chinese. Pre-existing, unchanged, noted in
   the README caveats. `validate_xml` does not object.
4. **The Dutch tier of Matthew is incomplete and OCR-error-prone** — the
   README's long-standing warning, retained and made prominent.

*(The first pass's item 3, a `_prettify` defect report, is withdrawn — see §4.)*

## 9. README

Rewritten again for the corrected verdict. It now leads with what the two
tiers mean here: `original` is Gravius's page, `standard` is the same text
minus line-break hyphens and **nothing else** — a reading tier, not a
transliteration — with the 1761/190 split stated so a user knows exactly how
much the tiers differ. It states plainly that the corpus has **no `PHON` at
any level** and why (no known phonemic transcription of Gravius's orthography),
explicitly disclaiming the "corpus is unimportant" reading, and notes that the
blank `standards.csv` entry is consistent: a standard tier without a designated
standard orthography scheme.

It also carries: a contents table (files, verses, both tiers, tokens,
translation counts, absence of PHON/W/M/audio); the retained source notes and
versification analysis; the "Line-break hyphens" section, now distinguishing
`hyphen_removals.csv` (**applied** — it defines the standard tier) from the
111-entry hand worklist (provenance only), with the evidence for keeping the
merges out of the original tier; full reproduction documentation — the
snapshot's role, the single `make_xml.sh` entry point with its arguments and
environment overrides, and step 0 plus both pipeline steps as runnable
commands, including the shared serializer and its declaration; why
`standardize.py`, `add_phonology.py` and `apply_manual_edits.py` are absent;
the sidecar policy; and the known caveats, including that the standard tier is
not the common orthography and must not be used for cross-corpus orthographic
comparison.

Per the README content policy it carries no sweep narrative and no rule
numbers.
